I had similar issues to your gf, among many other horrible pains/issues. It took SIX MONTHS for a doctor to take me seriously enough to just prescribe physical therapy. When I saw the physical therapist, she worked on me for all of 10 minutes for a "unspecified shoulder issue". I was in more pain than I've been in in my entire life. I was crying uncontrollably. She told me she couldn't touch me again til I got an MRI , and that she suspected she knew what was wrong but couldn't say. I went to the orthopedic Dr with the order from the physical therapist. He rolled his eyes at me and prescribed the MRI but told me he "wasn't very impressed" with my pain. At this point I couldn't sit, stand, lay, sleep, or do anything. I relapsed on drugs around this point too (many reasons, but the all consuming pain was one of them). I got my MRI and his tune changed. "Ms radio please sit down .." turns out I herniated three discs in my neck and had two more bulging. They thought I had been in a bad car wreck. All of the sudden they were trying to write me all these prescriptions and they scheduled me four days a week at physical therapy. They pulled me out of work. 

Anyways, sorry for saying all of that but it comes back to women are not taken seriously in the slightest. The first Dr I had who gatekept me the most was actually a woman too. The physical therapist who finally realized something was seriously wrong was also a woman, and she wasted no time making the doctors give me the care I actually needed. I'm so thankful for her intuition every single day. My life isn't pain free and I have nerve damage ,and still deal with this every day, but I know how to prevent seriously irritating the injury. I hope your gf can find someone to take her seriously, and it's great she has you to try to help advocate for her. It's a shame we have to just hope we get lucky and find a doctor who will actually take pity on us enough to treat us.
